requirements.name: go-module-command
requirements.text: The implementation language is Go, fixed by this Target's `TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md` and governed by `stack/go.md`.

requirements.name: decoder-contract
requirements.text: The program is a filter: read TOML from **stdin**, write tagged JSON to **stdout**, exit `0`.

requirements.name: parse-strings
requirements.text: **Scalars** — booleans, integers (including `0x`, `0o`, `0b`, underscores), floats (including `inf`, `nan`, exponents), basic and literal strings, then multi-line strings with their line-ending backslash and trimming rules.

requirements.name: parse-lexical-scalars
requirements.text: **Scalars** — booleans, integers (including `0x`, `0o`, `0b`, underscores), floats (including `inf`, `nan`, exponents), basic and literal strings, then multi-line strings with their line-ending backslash and trimming rules.

requirements.name: enforce-lexical-boundaries
requirements.text: **Invalid-input hardening** — control characters, bad UTF-8, duplicate keys, redefinition after an inline table, unterminated constructs.

requirements.name: parse-keys
requirements.text: **Keys** — bare, quoted, and dotted keys; the redefinition rules.

requirements.name: parse-tables
requirements.text: **Tables** — `[table]`, `[a.b.c]` implicit creation, `[[array of tables]]`, and the rules governing which of these may follow which.

requirements.name: parse-arrays-inline-tables
requirements.text: **Inline tables and arrays** — including nesting and the TOML 1.0 restriction that inline tables are closed to later extension.

requirements.name: parse-datetimes
requirements.text: **Datetimes** — offset, local datetime, local date, local time.

requirements.name: pass-conformance-suite
requirements.text: The goal is to pass every valid and every invalid case the installed suite supplies, with no case failed, errored, or skipped.

requirements.name: pin-conformance-version
requirements.text: The version setup_harness.sh installs. run_conformance.sh refuses a different one, so a passing verdict names a specific exam rather than whichever harness was on PATH.

requirements.name: build-and-run-conformance
requirements.text:
go build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder
DECODER="$PWD/toml-decoder" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh

requirements.name: run-conformance-suite
requirements.text: Run the upstream toml-test conformance suite against the built decoder.

requirements.name: require-decoder-command
requirements.text:
DECODER    decoder command. Required — this harness is language-neutral and
              deliberately has no default implementation language.

requirements.name: locate-test-harness
requirements.text: TOML_TEST  absolute path to the toml-test binary (default: found on PATH)

requirements.name: enforce-harness-version
requirements.text:
The suite's identity is part of the verdict. Without this, "the authoritative suite passed"
names no particular suite: whichever toml-test happened to be on PATH decided the run, and a
different version on a different machine is a different exam.

requirements.name: return-harness-verdict
requirements.text: # Exit code is the harness exit code: 0 only when every test passes.

requirements.name: install-toml-test-harness
requirements.text: One-time installation of the upstream toml-test conformance harness.

requirements.name: architecture-gate
requirements.text:
test -f go.mod
    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*require[[:space:](]' go.mod; then
      echo "go.mod declares a forbidden third-party dependency" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    go build ./cmd/toml-decoder

requirements.name: decoder-gate
requirements.text:
go build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder
    stage_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$stage_dir"' EXIT HUP INT TERM

    printf 'answer = 42\n' | ./toml-decoder >"$stage_dir/valid.json" 2>"$stage_dir/valid.err"
    test ! -s "$stage_dir/valid.err"
    python - "$stage_dir/valid.json" <<'PY'
import json
import sys

with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as stream:
    decoded = json.load(stream)
assert decoded == {"answer": {"type": "integer", "value": "42"}}
PY

    if printf 'answer = [\n' | ./toml-decoder >"$stage_dir/invalid.out" 2>"$stage_dir/invalid.err"; then
      echo "malformed TOML exited successfully" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    test ! -s "$stage_dir/invalid.out"
    test -s "$stage_dir/invalid.err"

requirements.text: Runs one slice of the authoritative suite.

if [ $# -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "usage: stage_test.sh <toml-test -run pattern>" >&2
  exit 2
fi

requirements.name: toml-document-basics
requirements.text:
* TOML is case-sensitive.
* A TOML file must be a valid UTF-8 encoded Unicode document.
* Whitespace means tab (0x09) or space (0x20).
* Newline means LF (0x0A) or CRLF (0x0D 0x0A).

A hash symbol marks the rest of the line as a comment, except when inside a
string.

requirements.name: key-value-pairs
requirements.text:
The primary building block of a TOML document is the key/value pair.

Keys are on the left of the equals sign and values are on the right. Whitespace
is ignored around key names and values. The key, equals sign, and value must be
on the same line (though some values can be broken over multiple lines).

requirements.name: strings
requirements.text:
There are four ways to express strings: basic, multi-line basic, literal, and
multi-line literal. All strings must contain only valid UTF-8 characters.

requirements.name: scalar-values
requirements.text:
Values must have one of the following types.

- [String](#string)
- [Integer](#integer)
- [Float](#float)
- [Boolean](#boolean)
- [Offset Date-Time](#offset-date-time)
- [Local Date-Time](#local-date-time)
- [Local Date](#local-date)
- [Local Time](#local-time)
- [Array](#array)
- [Inline Table](#inline-table)

requirements.name: dates-and-times
requirements.text:
To unambiguously represent a specific instant in time, you may use an [RFC
3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) formatted date-time with offset.

If you omit the offset from an [RFC 3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339)
formatted date-time, it will represent the given date-time without any relation
to an offset or timezone.

If you include only the date portion of an
[RFC 3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) formatted date-time, it will
represent that entire day without any relation to an offset.

If you include only the time portion of an [RFC
3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) formatted date-time, it will
represent that time of day without any relation to a specific day or any offset
or timezone.

requirements.name: arrays-and-inline-tables
requirements.text:
Arrays are square brackets with values inside. Whitespace is ignored. Elements
are separated by commas. Arrays can contain values of the same data types as
allowed in key/value pairs. Values of different types may be mixed.

Inline tables provide a more compact syntax for expressing tables. They are
especially useful for grouped data that can otherwise quickly become verbose.
Inline tables are fully defined within curly braces: `{` and `}`. Within the
braces, zero or more comma-separated key/value pairs may appear.

requirements.name: tables
requirements.text:
Tables (also known as hash tables or dictionaries) are collections of key/value
pairs. They are defined by headers, with square brackets on a line by
themselves.

The last syntax that has not yet been described allows writing arrays of tables.
These can be expressed by using a header with a name in double brackets. The
first instance of that header defines the array and its first table element, and
each subsequent instance creates and defines a new table element in that array.
The tables are inserted into the array in the order encountered.

requirements.name: toml-file-metadata
requirements.text:
TOML files should use the extension `.toml`.

When transferring TOML files over the internet, the appropriate MIME type is
`application/toml`.
